brief.question: Do explicit noncompact Gaussian exterior corrections pass independent controls and reproduce the actual mixed gravitational first responses within declared finite-grid thresholds?
brief.healthy: All structural comparisons pass. Coarse physical discrepancies are retained as diagnostics. Required physical and final-refinement comparisons pass only if the finest declared grid is adequate.
brief.noise: The earlier scalar inverse refinement established synthetic primitives only. A coarse diagnostic failure is allowed; it does not waive any finest-grid or structural requirement.
brief.worth_a_flag: Any required comparison failure, work-cap rejection, nonfinite value, or source/exterior mismatch is material. The first mixed-source levels may be underresolved; preserve a failed gate rather than relaxing tolerances.
brief.from_parent: The inverse-primitive parent passed 903 required comparisons in about 295 seconds. Full-mode noncompact adapters have not been timed; the new bounded workload may cost more.
brief.decided: One local CPU run, 1800-second wall limit, 8-GiB sampled memory ceiling. The initial attempt stopped at its 2-GiB memory guard; only that ceiling changes. No GPU or remote compute. No W2, u3, u4 or mixed-H6 acceptance is claimed by this run. All completed evidence is checkpointed. This is numerical inverse validation, not training; use only the declared control/level stages.
